title: Console request journey investigation - Acme Medical
summary: Walkthrough of Console tracing and request logs focused on reproducing an intermittent 504 path. Covered request playback, trace chaining, KV cache behavior, fallback routing, and required security artifacts for a pilot.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-12
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Ibrahim Khan (Acme SRE), Maya Lopez (Acme Platform), Ruth Chang (Acme CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Walked through a specific 504 incident, used request id 8f2b... to replay, showed how Console stitches traces across retries and model fallbacks. Discussed pilot scope and next steps to run a 2-week dedicated capacity pilot and security review timeline.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, this is Diego who is our solutions engineer, um we'll run through the Console trace and playback flow. Is the time still good? 
[00:12] Ibrahim Khan: Yes yep, we got an hour, we may run a little over, that's fine. Our day is packed but this is high priority.
[00:25] Diego Martinez: Quick agenda — reproduce the 504 from last week, show request playback and the tracechain, check KV cache hints, and then talk about mitigations and pilot details.
[00:37] Maya Lopez: Cool. For context our stack is Kubernetes EKS, we front Redwood requests through an internal API gateway, and we see occasional 504s at peak QPS, looks like KV cache misses correlate but not always.
[00:52] Lena Park: Got it. So we'll start from the trace view — Diego do you want to open the problematic request? Link: https://app.redwood.dev/console/trace/8f2b-... (shared)
[01:05] Diego Martinez: pulling it up now, um sometimes the transcript mislabels — okay here's the trace, you can see retries and a fallback to smaller model at 12:36:18. Notice the model variant available was quant-7b-fp4 and the fallback used quant-3b-int8.
[01:28] Ruth Chang: pause — how are you surfacing the fallback? Is that automatic or policy-driven? We only want fallback for non-PII paths.
[01:40] Diego Martinez: Good question, it's policy-driven; in your routing rules you'd set fallback to 'compatible-variant' and we can limit by route label to exclude sensitive flows. On the trace we keep a breadcrumb when fallback happens — sometimes the name is a little different in the transcription like 'quant' flagged as 'quantum', sorry for that, the real field is model_variant.
[01:58] Ibrahim Khan: On that trace I see a 'kv cash miss' note — that's 'kv cache' right? the export spelled it K V cash in the logs.
[02:10] Diego Martinez: yeah transcription is rough, but the Console shows cache hit/miss and TTL. Here you can see a spike in cold KV cache population after a scale event at 12:34.
[02:28] Lena Park: we also want to show playback — click 'Request Playback' button, that will replay the request against the pinned model version or a canary.
[02:40] Maya Lopez: If we replay, will it use live user data? We need it to sanitize PII.
[02:51] Diego Martinez: Playback has a 'sanitize' toggle and you can scrub entities — Redwood also offers a mask policy. We'll send the docs. (link: https://redwood.dev/docs/playback-sanitization)
[03:05] [screen share change noise]
[03:12] Diego Martinez: Starting playback now, it'll hit a sandboxed runner. Note the playback captured the same 504 path when we forced a degraded GPU pool. See the timeline: initial attempt -> retry -> fallback -> response with truncated tokens.
[03:36] Ibrahim Khan: Ok that matches our occurrence. The timing correlation with our autoscaler is interesting — did you see CPU/GPU utilization around the same timestamps?
[03:48] Diego Martinez: Yes there's an infra panel we can embed into the trace. It's here: shows GPU mem step-up and queue depth increase. There's also a 'batching' heatmap, sometimes heavy batching pushes latency over your SLO.
[04:04] Ruth Chang: You mentioned batching — can Redwood bound request size or force smaller batch windows for particular routes?
[04:16] Diego Martinez: Yep, you can set per-route batch windows and max tokens per-batch, and for Dedicated we give tighter controls. On Hosted you can do route priority to reduce batching latency.
[04:29] Maya Lopez: Do we need Dedicated to get strict low-latency? We're trying to avoid big commitments unless the pilot proves it.
[04:40] Lena Park: For a pilot we usually start hosted with reserved burst capacity; if the SLA/throughput needs are strict then Dedicated is next step. We'll map out criteria.
[04:52] [05:00] Diego Martinez: Going back to tracechain — the trace id jumps between services: gateway -> redwood-api -> inference runtime -> kvstore. Console stitches request ids using a short hash, sometimes the id is truncated in transcription like '8 f 2 b' but it's the same value.
[05:18] Ibrahim Khan: Is there an exportable CSV for a batch of traces? We want to correlate with our own logs.
[05:28] Diego Martinez: yes you can export trace sets with JSON/CSV. We'll attach a sample export in the follow-up.
[05:40] Maya Lopez: action item for us: we'll pull 10 samples for the week where 99th p95 latency exceeds threshold.
[05:50] Lena Park: great — we'll help with the filter query. (note: shared query link)
[06:02] [06:15] Diego Martinez: showing the error analysis tab now — shows stack traces and error codes. The 504s in your case are often annotated with 'runtime-timeout' and 'kv-miss+fallback', the console suggests possible root causes and the top hypothesis is batching-induced head-of-line blocking.
[06:40] Ibrahim Khan: That head-of-line sounds plausible. Could you show the replay where you reduce batch window from 50ms to 10ms?
[06:52] Diego Martinez: yep replaying with 10ms, looking... response time cut by ~40% but cost per token goes up. There is a cost/latency tradeoff dashboard that shows token cost delta.
[07:10] Ruth Chang: cost vs latency is exactly the concern; we'd need a runbook for acceptable cost increase.
[07:22] Lena Park: we can simulate the traffic shape and produce an expected cost delta for the pilot. We'll include per-route estimates in the POC template.
[07:34] [07:45] Maya Lopez: On security — we need SOC 2 type II, KMS key integration, RBAC for logs, and audit trails for playback. Can Redwood surface playback as an auditable event?
[07:58] Lena Park: Yes audit logs include playback events with user id, timestamp, and trace id. KMS and customer-managed keys are supported for Private and Dedicated; Hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys unless you provision a VPC/private deployment.
[08:18] Diego Martinez: also note we can filter playback to remove PII and generate a redacted artifact — the redaction is recorded in the audit.
[08:32] Ibrahim Khan: Great. Next, can you show a case where model fallback masked the real root cause? We worry fallbacks can hide infra issues.
[08:45] Diego Martinez: Good point. here's a trace where fallback to a smaller quantized model returned a faster response but masked a runtime error in the primary path — Console highlights these and you can toggle 'show hidden errors' to unmask underlying failures.
[09:02] Maya Lopez: That is helpful.
[09:10] [09:26] Diego Martinez: one more thing — request logs support correlation keys from your gateway. We saw you weren't sending 'x-correlation-id' in some requests, so Console generated internal ids; recommending you pass through your IDs to keep traces aligned.
[09:40] Ibrahim Khan: We can flip that on the gateway side.
[09:46] Ruth Chang: From a compliance perspective, what's retention for logs in Hosted? We may need 13 months for audits.
[09:58] Lena Park: Hosted default is 90 days but we have extended log retention add-ons; Dedicated and Private customers can set retention per policy. We'll include pricing for that.
[10:12] [10:30] Diego Martinez: let's run through a mock triage: step 1 identify trace -> step 2 check cache hit/miss -> step 3 check batching & queue -> step 4 reproduce with playback -> step 5 consider routing/priority or canary rollback.
[10:54] Maya Lopez: For the replay environment, can we hook to our staging models rather than Redwood's sandbox?
[11:05] Diego Martinez: For Private/Dedicated you can pin to your own model versions or a staging tag; hosted can route to a 'customer-managed' private runner if set up.
[11:20] Ibrahim Khan: we also want to test a canary that only affects 1% of traffic, is that supported at route level?
[11:30] Lena Park: yes per-route rollout with weights, and Console shows canary diff metrics and alerts.
[11:38] [11:50] Diego Martinez: small demo: creating a canary for /billing route now — setting weight 1% and a rollback policy if 5xx frequency increases by >2x.
[12:06] Maya Lopez: nice. How are alerts surfaced? Slack, webhook, PagerDuty?
[12:16] Diego Martinez: All of the above. Alert actions can also kick off automatic rollback policies.
[12:26] Ruth Chang: Can we set RBAC so only certain teams can trigger playback? We want to limit who can run replays because of PII exposure.
[12:38] Lena Park: yes role-based controls for playback and redaction required. We'll share our RBAC matrix.
[12:50] [13:00] Diego Martinez: Sharing the POC template now (link: https://redwood.dev/poctemplate/acme-poc). It has sections: success metrics, QPS shape, sample prompts, security checklist.
[13:14] Ibrahim Khan: We'll fill the sample prompts but need help to anonymize production prompts.
[13:28] Lena Park: Redwood can help with masking — we also have a small utility to fuzz sample prompts.
[13:38] [13:45] Diego Martinez: quick detour — error stack shows 'oom during attention' in one trace, that tends to happen with long contexts, we recommend context shortening or KV caching for repeated prefixes.
[13:58] Maya Lopez: We do have long contexts sometimes for threaded conversations.
[14:08] Diego Martinez: KV cache/two-pass architecture can help — Console shows KV cache hot keys and you can pre-warm on deploy.
[14:20] Ibrahim Khan: Pre-warm sounds useful — is there an API to seed cache on deploy?
[14:30] Diego Martinez: Yes there's a cache priming API and a pre-warm job; we'll share doc link.
[14:40] Ruth Chang: For audit, does the pre-warm job metadata include who initiated and what keys were primed?
[14:52] Lena Park: Yes it's auditable.
[15:00] [15:10] Diego Martinez: we've reached the part where we discuss SLA considerations. For Dedicated you get 99.95 p99 latencies with committed capacity; Hosted SLA depends on plan.
[15:28] Maya Lopez: timeline question — we are aiming for a 6-week pilot and then a decision. Is that typical?
[15:38] Lena Park: yes 4–8 weeks pilot is common. We'll provide a pilot plan and acceptance criteria.
[15:48] Ibrahim Khan: Ok can we discuss data residency? Our PHI must stay in us-east-1.
[15:58] Lena Park: for Hosted we can pin region to us-east-1; for strict controls Private (VPC) or on-prem is possible.
[16:10] [16:20] Diego Martinez: showing trace correlation with your Prometheus metrics now — console can ingest your metrics for side-by-side view.
[16:34] Maya Lopez: Great. How about synthetic load testing, is that included?
[16:44] Diego Martinez: We run synthetic load against your pilot config for a nominal fee; we can set QPS shape to mimic spikes.
[16:56] Ruth Chang: we'll need that for validation.
[17:06] [17:20] Lena Park: Let's capture next steps and action items.
[17:28] Diego Martinez: I'll attach the trace export and the sample CSV, also the POC template I linked earlier.
[17:36] Ibrahim Khan: I'll pull 10 traces and share them via the worksheet.
[17:44] Maya Lopez: I'll coordinate legal/security; need SOC 2 report and encryption SLA.
[17:52] Ruth Chang: I'll review the pilot acceptance criteria.
[17:58] Lena Park: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with timeline and pricing. Quick recap: run a 2-week hosted pilot with reserved burst capacity, run absorption testing, and then evaluate Dedicated if needed. We'll send security artifacts and a proposed pilot SOW.

Transcript end.
action_items: Diego Martinez - Attach trace export JSON + sample CSV - 2026-03-13
Lena Park - Send POC template and pilot SOW and pricing - 2026-03-13
Lena Park - Share SOC2 report and encryption/KMS docs - 2026-03-14
Ibrahim Khan - Provide 10 example trace IDs and sample prompts - 2026-03-15
Maya Lopez - Coordinate legal/security follow-up and T&Cs - 2026-03-16
next_steps: Schedule pilot kickoff (2-week hosted reserved burst) - propose dates 2026-03-22 to 2026-04-05
Run synthetic load test and provide cost/latency delta report
Security team to review SOC2 and KMS options
Set up demo account with correlation-id passthrough enabled
